description_en: The monastery is built on a two-stepped raised plinth. Carvings of wisdom bearers adorn the doorframe which is flanked by two blind windows bearing images of Bhairava. A colonnaded phalca can be found to the left side of the courtyard's entrance. To its right stands a statue of Mahakala, as well as a small niche on the wall worshipped as Hanuman.The main shrine is located at the northern side of the south wing and is accessible via a brass-clad door. An Ashoka caitya, a dharmadhātu maṇḍala, and a dharmadhātu jinālaya caitya are aligned along the north-south axis. The west wing was dismantled in the early 1980s and replaced with a single-storey structure that functioned as a primary school (Gutschow 2011, 726). This school also made use of the eastern wing. The school has since moved, and the space left behind on the western side is now used to store musical instruments. Local residents sometimes use this area to hold feasts. They also use the first floor gallery for gatherings and special events.Locke (1985, 191) describes two large stone lions flanking the main entrance. However, at present (writing in 2018) neither statues of lions nor bells can be found here although these objects are a common feature of bahās and bahīs. Instead, two small wooden phalcas are fixed on both sides of the main entrance. The carved wooden door of the Bahi is flanked by two blind windows depicting Bhairava.The shrine of kvāpādyaḥ is in the southern wing of the monastic building, and its brass-clad entrance is on the northern side. The wall to the right of the entrance has been painted with an image of Sāriputra, and another painting can be found to the left, this time of Maudgalyāyana. Stone inscriptions are attached to the wall on either side of the entrance. There is no toraṇa above the door, but one can find images of five Buddhas and Mañjuśrī to its left and Ṣaḍakṣarī to its right. The sanctum of the kvāpādyaḥ shrine contains a statue of Akṣobhya Buddha facing north. According to Locke, it was once possible to circumambulate the cella.The 2015 earthquake heavily damaged this Bahi and so the local people demolished its upper floor and covered it with temporary CGI sheets. The monastery has been renovated by INTACH India, and officially inaugurated on 22 March 2024, in the presence of the Indian ambassador. The old struts and pillars have been replaced by new carvings, the whereabouts of the historic material are unknown as per local residents response. The former garden, including a small field for begetables and fruit trees has been replaced by a lawn with a festival platform.
description_ne: ललितपुरमा रहेका बहीहरूमध्ये यसलाई सबैभन्दा जेठो बही मानिन्छ । त्यसैले यसलाई ज्येष्ठवर्ण महाविहार पनि भनिन्छ । पहिले नै जीर्ण अवस्थामा रहेको यस बहीलाई सन् 2015 को भूकम्पले निकै क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ ।यो बहीमा पस्ने ढोकासम्म पुग्न सिंढीहरू बनाइएका छन् । लक (1975: 191) ले सिंढीको दायाँबायाँ सिह राखिएका छन् भनी लेखेपनि हाल त्यहाँ सिंह राखिएका छैनन् । मूलढोकाको दायाँबायाँ बस्नको लागि फलेचा बनाइएका छन् । मूलढोकामाथि बार्दली भएकोमा भूकम्पले भत्किएको छ । मूलढोकाबाट भित्र पसेपछि दायाँ (पश्चिमतिर) महाकालको मूर्ति र हनुमानको प्रतीक स्वरूप खोपा बनाइएको छ । भूकम्पले बहीको चारैतर्फको माथिल्लो तल्ला भत्किएको छ । त्यसैले बहीको द्य:छेँको छानामाथि रहने पुल (Tower) र बहीको चारैतर्फ हुने बार्दली पनि अब छैन । अहिले रेलिङ्ग लगाएर जस्तापाता राखिएको छ । बहीको भुमितल्लामा गर्भगृहभित्र उत्तराभिमुख अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको मूर्ति राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहको बाहिर सिंह, घण्टा पनि छैनन् । लकले अनुसन्धान गर्दा गर्भगृह परिक्रमा गर्ने प्रदक्षिणापथ थियो, तर अहिले त्यो पनि बन्द भइसकेको छ । गर्भगृह पस्ने ढोका पित्तलले मोडेको छ । ढोकाको माथि तोरण पनि छैन । ढोकाको दायाँबायाँ सारिपुत्र र मौदगल्यायनको चित्र लेखिएको छ । ढोकामाथि बीचमा पञ्चबुद्ध, दायाँ षडक्षरी र बायाँ मञ्जुश्रीको चित्र लेखिएको छ ।विहार परिसरमा अशोक चैत्य, धर्मधातु मण्डल र धर्मधातु जिनालय चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । यो वज्राचार्यहरूको बही हो । संघ सदस्य कम हुँदै जाँदा अहिले एउटा परिवार मात्र बाँकी छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Donation of bricks for the courtyard

historical_events.event_description: The land of Luchẽnani (to the eastern side of the Bahī) belonged to that monastic building. It contained some houses with roofs made of straw. The roof of theākhāchẽ(a cultural house where musical instruments, masks and dresses are stored) was tiled by a group of volunteers led by Narami Bhāvo.
The entrance of thekvāpādyaḥshrine is clad in brass. Kājīlāl and his wife Sānu donated funds for this work to be carried out in memory of their deceased father Jitamā.
Consecration of thecaturvyūha caityaoutside the Bahī during the reign of King Śrīnivāsa Malla. This was conducted by Harinandan Duwāra Bhāro and Binatā Mayi.
